clue.text: Medical report on victim of shooting incident

definitions.meaning: an official statement on a patient's condition, as issued about a sick public figure
read as two words, someone with a slug lodged in them after being shot

explanation.surface: A doctor issues an update on the condition of someone who was shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A short official statement of news, such as a hospital's update on a patient, is a bulletin; split, the word describes someone who has been hit.

clue.text: Mulled wine for His Lordship

definitions.meaning: a hot spiced drink of port or wine with oranges
a senior cleric of the Church of England, addressed as My Lord

explanation.definitionFit: A drink of spiced warmed port shares its name with the senior churchman addressed as My Lord.

clue.text: Appeared to be satisfactory in dole distribution

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
a distribution scatters things about, so the letters are dealt out afresh

parts.note: OK means satisfactory or all right

explanation.surface: Something seemed acceptable in the way unemployment benefit was handed out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dole' is British slang for unemployment benefit; here it is just letters to be dealt out.
explanation.definitionFit: To have seemed or given the impression of something is to have looked it.

clue.text: But expect to be knocked into shape

indicators.note: knocking something into shape means forcing it into a new form, so the letters take a new order

explanation.surface: Someone hopes for something but must expect to be bullied into fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be knocked into shape' rearranges EXPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce an exclusion, as in all but one or all save one.

clue.text: Laughing uncontrollably this month over ticklish sensations

parts.note: inst., short for instant, is old business shorthand for this month
itches are irritating, tickling feelings on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone has been in fits of laughter all month from being tickled.
explanation.walkthrough: INST, for instant, was used in letters to mean this month, as in your letter of the 5th inst.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for helpless laughter compares it to the sharp pain of a side stitch.

clue.text: About to pull back the gaoler

indicators.note: back tells us to read the whole run of letters from the end to the start

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about or concerning, as in business letters
to draw is to pull, as a cart or a curtain

explanation.surface: A prison guard is about to drag someone back to the cells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run RE + DRAW into WARDER. 'Gaoler' is the British spelling of jailer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison officer in charge of inmates is called a warder in British usage.

clue.text: Jelly for two silver-headed artists

annotationWithheld.why: Jelly for two silver-headed artists (4-4): silver AG heading artists RA, doubled, gives AGRAAGRA not AGARAGAR; no standard abbreviation for artists gives AR, so the parse as held does not reach the answer

clue.text: Drive out from the House of Hades

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, the equivalent of Hades
a lodge is a house, such as a gatehouse or a hunting lodge

explanation.surface: Someone is expelled from the underworld god's home.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis, the Roman underworld god, stands for Hades, so the house of Hades is Dis's lodge.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something or someone from its position is to dislodge it.

clue.text: He renders an account to military caretaker

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
a porter looks after a building, as a doorkeeper or caretaker does

explanation.surface: A soldier-caretaker submits a report on the building.
explanation.definitionFit: A journalist who gives an account of events is a reporter.

clue.text: A theatrical action it displays to advantage

definitions.text: A theatrical action it displays to advantage

parts.words: A theatrical action it displays to advantage
parts.note: split in two, a stage performance plus a lawsuit gives a theatrical legal action, while the whole is a glass cabinet that sets off its contents well

explanation.surface: A dramatic lawsuit puts something on display to good effect.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-fronted display cabinet, or any setting that presents something at its best, is a showcase.

clue.text: Tom is out of bed and dressing

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
is shortened to 's, as in it's
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: A man named Tom has got out of bed and is putting his clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name but it is a male cat. 'is' contracts to the S of 's.
explanation.definitionFit: Catsup is an old spelling of ketchup, a sauce or condiment, which counts as a dressing for food.

clue.text: Provide a new design, and be given extra money

indicators.note: giving the letters a new design means arranging them in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone redesigns a project and receives a bonus for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new design' rearranges PROVIDE plus A into OVERPAID.
explanation.definitionFit: To be paid too much is to receive more money than is due.

clue.text: Socialist workers

definitions.meaning: the UK's main left-of-centre party, founded by trade unions

explanation.definitionFit: The British Labour Party is the main socialist party, and the work force as a body is called labour.

clue.text: The merchandise as yet isn't moving at all

parts.note: a shop's stock is the merchandise it holds
still means up to now or as yet

explanation.surface: The goods have yet to sell and are not shifting at all.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a predicate: the thing is stock-still.
explanation.definitionFit: Being completely motionless, without any movement, is being stock-still.

clue.text: A dear little fish, but it needs a sharp fork

parts.note: something dear and little is cute
to fish with rod and line is to angle

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing a sweet little fish needs a sharp fork to eat it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fish' looks like a noun but is the verb, giving ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lines forking apart at less than ninety degrees form an angle under a right angle, so a sharp fork is witty for it.

clue.text: Disorderly rush for an emergency take-off

definitions.meaning: a hurried struggle as people jostle to get somewhere first
the rapid launch of fighter aircraft to meet a threat

explanation.definitionFit: A disorderly scrum to get somewhere is a scramble, as is the RAF's word for fighters launching fast.

clue.text: Decongestant given to trendy Henry by social worker

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in crowd
Hal is a nickname for Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
an ant is a social insect, the classic worker

explanation.surface: A fashionable man named Henry is given a cold remedy by a social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' looks like a welfare officer but is an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine breathed in to clear a blocked nose is an inhalant.

clue.text: Demand in Jerusalem for the onion

indicators.note: in means the demand goes inside the city's name

parts.note: Sion is an old spelling of Zion, a name for Jerusalem
a call is a demand, as in a call for action

explanation.surface: In Jerusalem people clamour for onions.
explanation.walkthrough: SION is the older spelling of Zion, the biblical name for Jerusalem.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion or shallot, a kind of onion.

clue.text: Study physics, for instance, and gain moral awareness

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
physics is one example of a science

explanation.surface: Studying physics leads someone to an ethical awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner sense of right and wrong that guides behaviour is one's conscience.

clue.text: Glass of beer with flipped egg-flip results in gibberish

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

indicators.note: flipped means the drink's name is turned end to end

parts.note: egg-flip is another name for eggnog, so nog

explanation.surface: A pint of beer plus a knocked-over eggnog leaves someone talking nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' turns NOG into GON. 'Jar' is British slang for a drink of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unintelligible or specialist language is jargon, close in sense to nonsense talk.

clue.text: Finch gets public house included in lease

indicators.note: included in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to let is to lease out property
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A pub finds itself part of a property rental agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown songbird of the finch family.

clue.text: Tax the family

definitions.meaning: a verb meaning to put heavy pressure on, as in stretching resources
a line of descent, breed or stock

explanation.definitionFit: To tax is to overstretch, which is to strain; a breed or ancestral line is also a strain.

clue.text: Butler getting in beer ideal for farmers

indicators.note: getting in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
Rab Butler was a British Conservative statesman known by the nickname Rab

explanation.surface: A butler bringing in beer is just what farm workers want.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butler' looks like a servant but is the politician R.A. Butler, known as Rab.
explanation.definitionFit: Land suitable for ploughing and growing crops is arable, so it suits farmers.

clue.text: Writer has to make the attempt first

definitions.text: Writer has to make the attempt first

parts.words: Writer has to make the attempt first
parts.note: a writer of short prose pieces must first make an attempt, since those pieces take their name from an old verb meaning to try

explanation.surface: An author must try before succeeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of short prose compositions, called essays from the old word for a try, is an essayist.

clue.text: Undergarment given to Elizabeth back in South America

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

indicators.note: back says the short name is read from end to start

parts.note: Liz is a short form of Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A woman named Elizabeth is handed a bra on returning to South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Brazil is the largest country located in South America.

clue.text: Chaste young lady goes to Iowa from another state

parts.note: a chaste young woman is a virgin
IA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Iowa

explanation.surface: A pure young woman moves from one US state to another, starting in Iowa.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is one of the United States, a different one from Iowa.

clue.text: Scope for former partner to get temporary accommodation

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a tent is shelter that is put up and taken down

explanation.surface: Someone's ex is given room to stay in a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: Range or reach, how far something goes, is its extent.

clue.text: Marine organisms add great weight to ship's timber

parts.note: a plank is a long board used in building a ship's hull or deck
a ton is a heavy unit of weight

explanation.surface: Loading a heavy load onto a ship's woodwork somehow involves tiny sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny drifting plants and animals of the sea are collectively plankton.
